prompt:
A delivery van is travelling along a straight horizontal road at a steady velocity of 22.0 m s^-1. The driver applies the brakes, producing a constant deceleration of 4.40 m s^-2 until the van stops.
(a) Calculate the time taken for the van to come to rest. [1 mark]
(b) Calculate the distance travelled by the van while braking using:
(i) an equation of constant acceleration; [1 mark]
(ii) the area under a sketch of the velocity-time graph. [1 mark]
hints: For part (a), use v = u + at with u = 22.0 m s^-1, v = 0, and a = -4.40 m s^-2.
For part (b)(i), choose a formula such as v^2 = u^2 + 2as or s = 0.5(u + v)t.
For part (b)(ii), sketch a triangle from v = 22.0 m s^-1 to 0 over the stopping time.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: In part (a), apply v = u + at: 0 = 22.0 + (-4.40)t => t = 5.00 s [1 mark].
Step 3: In part (b)(ii), sketch a right-angled triangle with base 5.00 s and height 22.0 m s^-1. Area = 0.5 x 5.00 x 22.0 = 55.0 m [1 mark].
Step 4: Both representations confirm the identical stopping distance of 55.0 m.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored independently to test reconciling equation-based and graph-based solutions.
